newsitem.title: TURKEY: Saudi barley demand to increase - U.S. official.
newsitem.headline: Saudi barley demand to increase - U.S. official.

text.p: Saudi Arabia, currently keeping world grain markets on edge over a large barley purchase, may increase its strategic imports of the grain in the future, a U.S. agriculture official said on Monday.

Mark Sloan, agriculture counsellor at the U.S. embassy in Turkey, told a grains conference that cuts in subsidies to Saudi farmers would increase the kingdom's reliance on world markets, despite Middle East grain demand having stabilised this decade.
Saudi Arabia is the world's largest barley importer and has a strong influence over world prices for the feed grain.

"We see that total demand for feed grain in the Middlle East has stabilised after a period of rapid growth in the 1970s and 1980s," Sloan told the 2nd World Grain and Feed Conference in Antalya, southern Turkey.

"Saudi Arabia has historically accounted for over half of the region's feed grain demand, and with recent reductions in barley subsidies, is expected to increase imports -- a fact we were reminded of last week with the very large barley tender which that country issued," he said.
He gave no figures for the expected demand increase.
Saudi Arabia tendered last week for 1.72 million tonnes of barley for October-December delivery.
Grain traders said earlier on Monday the country was lining up actual purchases of some 1.4 million tonnes.
The International Grains Council predicts Saudi barley imports will pick up to 3.5 million tonnes this season (July/June) after dipping to 3.2 million tonnes in 1995/96.
Imports in 1993/94 and 1994/95 were 4.3 million and 4.2 million tonnes respectively.

World barley export prices have fallen as low as $130 per tonne since peaking around $200 per tonne in the world grain price explosion this year. But current prices are closer to $140 in the wake of the Saudi tender, traders said.
French barley prices were fairly firm on Monday ahead of the Saudi tender results expected later in the day.
